- `overpay_repayment_plan`: every clause carried in `repayment_plan_rule` (agreement; status condition established/in recovery with the record read; retired item 3; due dates; missed installment/default with the missed-payment measure spelled out; current plan vs referral and offsets; several overpayments under the recovery order); per-tier figures in `repayment_plan_terms_by_classification` (25/25/25/25/50/75; 60/60/60/48/36/24; 30; 15; 10; 2/2/2/2/1/1) — equal to the variant parameters.
- `overpay_evt_penalty_interest`: clauses (1)–(6) in force and (7) retired in `fraud_penalty_interest_and_fees_rule`; figures in `fraud_penalty_and_interest_rates`.
- `overpay_evt_recovery` and `overpay_agg_recovery_priority`: carried in `recovery_by_offset_repayment_and_refund`, `recovery_sharing_across_open_overpayments`, `offset_share_and_application_order`, `payment_channels_fees_and_refund_terms` (status table, offsets, application order incl. fees, refund, paid in full, employer credit; designated/undesignated/offset/intercept sharing; open-overpayment order with the measure's tie-break).

## kb_to_source

- Every normative sentence in the 27 documents carrying this task's four policies (four hubs, four baselines, 19 factor documents) and in the base documents listed above traces to a source rule sentence, a ladder, a measure definition, a lifecycle transition or a variant parameter. Interpretive notes ("Exactly 60 days falls in the middle row", "A first installment due date has passed when it is earlier than the handling date", "The channel is never taken from the return entry itself", "Each threshold belongs to the lower tier") are entailed readings of the source's comparisons, not new law.
- Additions / rewrites / omissions: none found.
- Cross-problem operational guidance ("if unmet, first call …", a resolving tool beside a prerequisite sentence): none. Each tool name occurs only in its own hub (scripted check: `book_returned_payment_fee_10cb479c` only in `returned_payment_fee_booking`; `pay_overpayment_arrears_d9b1e543` only in `defaulted_plan_arrears_payment`; `reinstate_repayment_plan_54c54ed5` only in `repayment_plan_reinstatement`; `set_up_repayment_plan_0b609272` only in `new_repayment_plan_setup`).
- Opening world state written as policy fact: none; every example is marked hypothetical and none uses this task's customer, ids, dates or amounts.

### Observations (do not change the verdict)

- O1 (arrears assembly seam). The source pins "the installment part, after any reduction, plus the fees that join, limited to the penalty standing unpaid". The KB states the cap as a property of the arrears payment as such (`plan_arrears_amount` ¶1 "it never exceeds the penalty standing unpaid") and the fees as "added to the arrears payment on top of its installment part" (`returned_installment_fees_in_arrears`), which together entail the source order; but the baseline worksheet takes the cap at line 9 before any factor applies, so a reader who treats the worksheet's line 9 as final and then adds fees could cap first. Not triggered in this task (138.00 against 521.90 of penalty unpaid). Recorded as a readability seam, not an omission.

## dependency_form

- Prerequisite sentences: each of the three carried verbatim in its blocked policy's hub, in state form, with a same-form restatement in the same section that names only the record field (plan status / repayment entry / fee entry). None is restated as an action; none names a tool, a policy or another document; none appears in a second document.
- Depended-on documents describe the waited-on states in the sentences' own words: "from defaulted to current" (reinstatement hub), "recorded on the overpayment's ledger as a repayment received" (arrears hub), "the overpayment's ledger carries a returned-payment fee for that returned repayment" (fee hub). Each was reached from the records' and sentences' words, not from phrasing borrowed from the blocked document. All four hops were marked state-derived in the blind answer; none pre-solved.
- No dependency table, checklist, route, ordered cross-problem procedure, wrong-vs-right contrast or cross-problem example anywhere in the corpus.
- Titles/openings: general subjects ("Setting Up a Repayment Plan on Benefit Overpayment Accounts — Console Reference", "Reinstating a Defaulted Repayment Plan", "Arrears Payment on a Defaulted Repayment Plan — … Payment Line", "Returned-Payment Fee on Benefit Overpayment Accounts — Console Reference"); none mirrors the task's situation.
- Factor documents: none says which tier a customer falls on, none names the computation document or another factor; computation documents carry no "unless otherwise provided"-type hint. (`return_lookback_period_anchoring` decides the look-back that `repeat_return_surcharge` reads; the two share only the business term "return look-back period", which is how the source itself nests the method factor — no pointer.)
- Policy-side note (Step 4, not a KB verdict): the arrears hub opens "A claimant whose repayment plan … has defaulted may bring the plan back to standing by paying its arrears." This is the arrears policy's own rule sentence (verbatim in `overpay_ext_plan_arrears.rule`), so the KB must carry it; it does tell the reader what the arrears payment is for, which leans toward the arrears→reinstatement relation from the depended-on side. Its source is the policy layer.

**Verdict: PASS** (no KB-EXPLICIT RED).
